# Brief for the coach: the 2 November program draft, dry run and current week

## Where things stand

The program in force is version 1, "Five compounds around the PT Tuesday", adopted 1 November 2026 as Joe's first program on this engine, emphasis hypertrophy, home as the default location. A block opened the same day and the rotation is at week A.

The draft dated 2 November started life as a straight copy of version 1: the first dry run found nothing changed and nothing to fill. I then made three edits to it (described below), re-ran the dry run, and that is what the rest of this brief reports. The check also pulled Hevy first and found nothing new between 21:05 and 21:15 on 2 November: no new workouts, weigh-ins, routines or folders.

## The program as it stands (unchanged parts)

Six training days, Thursday off. Two-week rotation, A and B, identical except Tuesday:

- Monday: overhead press, back and arms, 75-minute budget
- Tuesday: PT session at the gym; week A chest and back (estimated 6 chest sets, 6 lat sets, 3 biceps sets), week B legs and core (estimated 6 quad, 4 glute, 4 abdominal sets)
- Wednesday: pull-up volume and core, 75 minutes
- Friday: strict pull-up test, squat and legs, 75 minutes
- Saturday: bench, back and arms, 90 minutes
- Sunday: deadlift and legs, 90 minutes
- Plus two standing optional sessions outside the schedule: the kettlebell circuit and the daily hang.

Weekly dose target: 10 hard sets per muscle. Per lift: bench 5, overhead press 5, deadlift 4, back squat 5, pull-up (see the change below). Deload policy: a block runs at most 6 hard weeks, the light week cuts 40 % of sets and 0 % of load, caps every set at RPE 8, and tests the priority lifts.

Key lines, exactly as written:

- Overhead press (Monday): warm-ups of 5 and 3, one top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 sets of 6 at 85 % of the top set, 3 minutes' rest.
- Chest-supported dumbbell row: 4 sets of 8–12 at RPE 8. Lateral raise and rear-delt fly: 3 sets of 12–15 at RPE 8 each, paired.
- Wednesday: 2 activation sets of 6–8 scapular pull-ups at RPE 5; 3 sets of 2–4 negative pull-ups at RPE 8 with a 4–5 second lower (lengthen to 6 s, then 8 s, then add the vest once every set hits 4); 4 sets of 5–8 band pull-ups at RPE 8 (lighter band once every set hits the top); 2 flexed-arm hangs of 20 s; 3 sets of 10–15 lying leg raises paired with 4 suitcase carries of 30 s; 3 sets of 10–15 single-leg calf raises.
- Friday: one strict pull-up single at RPE 10 (one attempt, same grip every time); back squat warm-ups of 5, 3, 2, a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 sets of 5 at 85 %; Romanian deadlift 3 sets of 6–10; split squat 3 sets of 8–12; seated dumbbell press 3 sets of 8–12 paired with calf raises 3 sets of 10–15; ab wheel 3 sets of 6–12. All at RPE 8.
- Saturday: bench warm-ups of 8, 5, 3, a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 sets of 6 at 85 %; bent-over row 4 sets of 6–10; incline dumbbell press 3 sets of 8–12; dip negatives 3 sets of 3–5 with a 4–5 s lower (same lengthening rule); overhead triceps extension 3 sets of 10–15 paired with lateral raises 3 sets of 12–15. All at RPE 8.
- Sunday: deadlift and legs (the detail was cut from the readout; the farmer's walk starts at 50 lb per hand).

## The three edits in the draft, and what adopting would record

1. **The swing finisher leaves Monday and becomes its own conditioning session.** Monday's lifting previously ended with 8 sets of 10 kettlebell swings at 40 lb, one set at the top of each minute, RPE 7. That line is removed. In its place a new optional conditioning session, "Kettlebell swing EMOM", is scheduled beside Monday's lift in both rotation weeks, lift first. It runs every-minute-on-the-minute for 12 minutes, 12 swings each minute at 40 lb, aiming for RPE 7. When it comes in at or under that effort, the engine adds 2 minutes, up to a 16-minute cap, then reps can climb to 15. Twenty seconds' rest between sets is noted for the time estimate only; the clock sets the real rest.

2. **The pull-up gets a real weekly target.** Instead of a target of 1 (the single), the pull-up now carries a target of 10 hard sets a week, with negative pull-ups and band pull-ups counted toward it. The planned week supplies 3 negative sets, 7 band sets and the single. Counted variants add to the target only: they never stand in for the strict pull-up on a line, are never tested, and need not come first.

3. **The acknowledgement that excused the pull-up's target of 1 is removed**, because the warning it covered no longer fires.

The draft's stated reason: the engine's newer release lets a lift count its variants and lets a conditioning session sit beside a lifting day, so the swings get their own session instead of being tacked onto Monday.

Adopting records version 2 as an **amendment**: the block opened on 1 November continues, no reset, the rotation stays at week A. The dry run shows no defaults needing to be filled. Adopt writes nothing to Hevy. The Hevy routines only change when the next week plan is drafted and pushed, so the swing session will not appear on Joe's phone until that happens.

**What Joe must agree to:** the swings moving out of Monday's session into a separate 12-minute EMOM done the same day (ideally with a gap; see the stacking note below), 12 swings a minute at 40 lb growing to 16 minutes and 15 a minute; and that his pull-up progress is now judged against 10 counted sets a week rather than the single. He should also hear the deadlift question below before saying yes.

## Start loads the dry run confirmed

- Farmer's walk, Sunday: 50 lb per hand, recorded for Hevy as 45.36 kg (both hands together).
- Kettlebell swing, new EMOM session: 40 lb, 18.14 kg.
- Kettlebell swing, standing circuit: 40 lb, 18.14 kg.

## Session time estimates against budgets

Monday: budget 75 minutes, estimate 47 (was 58 before the swings moved out). Wednesday: 75, estimate 39. Friday: 75, estimate 65. Saturday: 90, estimate 65. Sunday: 90, estimate 65. The two PT sessions and the three optional sessions have no budget and no estimate. Nothing is over.

## Warnings on the draft (none blocks adoption)

**Deadlift target of 4 is below the 5–15 band.** The deadlift's 4 hard sets a week never changed; this warning only became visible once the pull-up's warning went away (the engine showed one at a time). What it means: at 4 sets the deadlift sits under the evidence band for a priority lift in a maintenance phase. What clears it: raise the target to 5 (and make the Sunday line deliver it), or write an acknowledgement stating why 4 is the right number for Joe — for instance the recovery cost of heavy pulls alongside squats, Romanian deadlifts and the occasional PT deadlift. It is unacknowledged right now, so I need the coach's call before the real adopt.

**Strict pull-up single under a "hold" scheme** sits outside the schemes expected on a priority lift (top-and-back-off, 5/3/1 waves, linear, assistance ladder, or double progression in 3–6 reps). This is already acknowledged in the draft: the single is the weekly measure while Joe's max is 1; the negatives and band pull-ups do the building; the strict line becomes real working sets once the test rep passes about five. Nothing to do.

**One Hevy routine has drifted from the week plan in force (dated 2 November).** On the first exercise, sets 5, 6 and 7 show different reps; on the second exercise, sets 1 to 3 show different weights. The readout names the routine only by its reference, not the session, so I cannot say for certain which day; the shape (seven-plus sets on the first exercise, three on the second) suggests Monday, where Joe did 8 reps rather than 6 on the back-offs. What it means: Hevy and the plan disagree, so the next workout may be logged against numbers the plan did not set. What clears it: the next week plan carrying an override, or the next push to Hevy, which rewrites the routine.

## A stacking note for the new swing session

The engine's rule flags a quality conditioning session (RPE 7 or higher) on the same day as any lifting session with under 6 hours between, and within 24 hours before a heavy squat or hinge day. The swings target RPE 7, so each week plan will likely raise a "drop suggested" warning on them unless they are done 6 hours or more after Monday's lift, or the warning is acknowledged. Separately, quality bouts (runs and conditioning together) are capped at 2 a week; Joe's three runs are easy, so the swings and the circuit are the two. The existing circuit already carries an acknowledgement that it is optional and done on a spare evening, never stacked on Monday — the same logic will need stating for the swings if Joe wants them on Monday evening.

## The week in force (plan dated 2 November): its warnings

These are on the current week plan, not the program draft, but the coach should know them:

- **Stall streaks (3 sessions in a row with no gain):** overhead press (top-set metric), rear-delt fly, band pull-up, negative pull-up, single-leg calf raise (both Wednesday and Friday), ab wheel, seated dumbbell press, bent-over row. Three flat sessions is the engine's threshold for noticing, not yet a reset. For the double-progression lines it means reps have not climbed within the range; for the overhead press it means the estimated max has not moved. Early in a block the usual answer is more sets or a closer look at effort; a reset only comes on a miss pattern.
- **Band pull-up rep range missed:** working set 4 logged 4 reps at RPE 10, so the load (band) holds this week.
- **RPE ceiling unchecked** (no usable estimated max, so the load is simply held): goblet squat at 20.25, chest-supported row at 34, suitcase carry at 4.25, seated dumbbell press at 22.5, split squat at 4.25. These clear on their own as logged sets build an estimate.
- **Suitcase carry anchor:** the last log recorded 0, which is not a rack row, so the engine anchored at 5 instead.
- **Back squat increment over step:** the pinned 170.5 is more than one rack row above the anchor's 118. Acknowledged: the anchor was a light home set, and the 13 October PT single at 100 kg puts 170.5 at about 75 % of the estimated max, below what the scheme itself proposed.
- **Circuit stacked on Monday:** acknowledged as above.

The older plan draft dated 1 November, checked for reference, carried one violation (a start load missing) and eight warning kinds including five RPE-ceiling-unchecked lines; it has been superseded by the plan in force.

## What Joe actually did on Monday 2 November

- Overhead press at 68 lb: 5, 6, 8, 8, 8 reps at RPE 7.5, 6, 6, 6, 6; estimated max 85. The back-offs were prescribed at 6 and went to 8 at RPE 6 — the weight was light for him.
- Chest-supported row at 20 lb per hand: 6, 12, 12 at RPE 8, 7, 7.5.
- Lateral raise at 5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 6, 7.5.
- Rear-delt fly at 7.5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 7, 8.
- Kettlebell swing at 40 lb: 8 sets of 10 at RPE 7 (last two at 7.5).
- Dead hang logged under the daily hang, no numbers recorded.

## Pull-up history since 1 September (the basis for the new target)

- 27 September 2026: band pull-ups 5, 5 at RPE 6.
- 26 October 2026: strict single, 1 rep at RPE 10; negatives 2, 2 at RPE 8 and 9; band pull-ups 6, 5, 5 at RPE 8.5 each.
- 1 November 2026: strict single, 1 rep at RPE 10; band pull-ups 6, 6, 5, 4 at RPE 8, 8.5, 9.5, 10.

None of these was matched to a planned session.

## Progress snapshot

- Pull-up: best 3 strict reps on 29 March 2026; 2 reps to go to the 5-rep target.
- Bench: estimated max 174.9; best 160.94 × 3 on 14 April 2026; 0.32 × bodyweight to go to 1.25 × BW.
- Overhead press: estimated max 85.15; best 93.0 × 5 on 10 July 2026; 0.24 × BW to go to 0.75 × BW.
- Deadlift: no current estimate; best 200.0 × 5 on 11 April 2026; 0.9 × BW to go to 2 × BW.
- Back squat: estimated max 231.48; best 220.46 × 1 on 13 October 2026; 0.32 × BW to go to 1.5 × BW.
- No stalls or resets recorded at block level; no cadence signals yet.
- Phase: maintenance, target 0.0 % of bodyweight a week, observed −0.13 % a week; the engine marks the maintenance target as not met (a slow drift down rather than holding). Until the coach calls it.

## Decision needed from the coach

1. Deadlift: raise the weekly target to 5, or give me the reason to keep 4 so it can be acknowledged.
2. Confirm Joe is happy with the swing EMOM as a separate Monday session and the pull-up target of 10 counted sets.
3. On both yeses, I run the real adopt (version 2, amendment, block continues, week A), then redraft and push the week so Hevy picks up the new swing routine and the drifted routine is rewritten.

first.text:
Here's what version 2 would change, everything it would set, and every caution attached — three of them, one of which needs your call before I record anything. Today's logged Monday workout stays exactly as it is.

**What changes**

*The swings.* They come off the end of Monday's lifting and become their own optional conditioning session, scheduled beside Monday's lift in both rotation weeks, lift first. Twelve minutes on the clock, 12 swings at the top of each minute with the 40 lb bell (18.14 kg), aiming for a 7. Whenever a session comes in at or under that effort, the clock grows by 2 minutes up to a 16-minute cap; once you're at 16, the reps climb toward 15 a minute. Monday's lifting drops from an estimated 58 minutes to 47 against your 75.

*The pull-up target.* My proposal is 10 hard sets a week, with negatives and band pull-ups counting toward it. The reasoning: the strict single is a measurement, not a dose — it tells us where you are, it doesn't build anything. The negatives and band work are what's actually building the lift, and they're the same muscles doing the same pattern under real load, so they belong in the count. Ten matches the weekly target for every other muscle, sits inside the band for a priority lift, and the week as written already delivers it: 3 negative sets, 7 band sets, plus the single on top. Your last two pull-up days show the band sets running from an 8 up to a 10 by the fourth set, which is a hard enough dose that I wouldn't push past 10 right now; if you'd rather err lighter while the negatives are new, 8 is defensible and I'd drop one band set on Wednesday. The note that used to excuse the old target of 1 goes away because nothing needs excusing anymore.

*The circuit.* Untouched, as you asked. On the second question: this week's plan still carries the note that the circuit is optional and lives on a spare evening. The rule hasn't softened — a hard conditioning bout within 6 hours of lifting, or in the 24 hours before a heavy squat or deadlift day, still gets a caution. As long as the circuit sits on its own evening it clears without a note; it only asks for one if it lands on a lifting day. The same applies to the new swing session: because it targets a 7 and sits beside Monday's lift, each week will ask about it unless there's a gap of 6 hours or more, or we state once that Monday evening is the plan. Tell me which you prefer and I'll write it that way. Your three easy runs don't count toward the two-hard-bouts-a-week cap, so the swings and the circuit are the two and that's fine.

**The one decision I need from you**

With the pull-up sorted, the deadlift's weekly target of 4 hard sets now shows as below the 5-set floor for a priority lift. That number hasn't changed; it was just hidden behind the pull-up before. My lean is to raise it to 5 and have Sunday deliver the extra set — the deadlift is your furthest lift from its goal, there's no current estimate because you haven't pulled heavy since April, and Sunday has 25 minutes spare. The case for keeping 4 is recovery: heavy pulls on Sunday follow Friday's squat top set and Romanian deadlifts, with the occasional PT leg day on Tuesday. If you'd rather hold at 4, I'll note that reason and it's settled. Either way I want it decided before this goes in rather than left hanging.

**Other things worth knowing, none of which block this**

The strict pull-up single is written as a hold rather than a progression scheme, which is deliberate and already explained in the program: it's the weekly test while your max is 1, and it becomes real working sets once the test rep passes about five.

Your Monday routine on your phone disagrees with the plan — the overhead press back-offs show 8 reps rather than the planned 6, and the row weights differ. That's just your phone remembering what you did. It gets rewritten the next time a week goes out. Related: those back-offs at 68 lb went to 8 reps at a 6, which says the weight was light for you. Not something to fix in this amendment, but I'll want to bring the top set up when the next week is drafted.

Several lines show three flat sessions in a row — overhead press, rear-delt fly, both pull-up variants, calf raises, ab wheel, seated press, bent-over row. Three sessions is just the point where it starts being noticed; a block that's one week old hasn't had time to move anything. Nothing to do yet.

Your bodyweight is drifting down about 0.13 % a week against a maintenance target of flat. Slow enough to watch rather than act on, but it's the kind of thing that would argue against a bigger deadlift dose if it continues.

**Recording this**

Version 2 is an amendment: the block that opened on 1 November continues, no reset, rotation stays at week A. Nothing goes to your phone when it's recorded; the swing session only appears there once the next week is drafted and sent, and I'll hold that until you say. After it's in, I'll confirm that the swings are no longer being counted as hard sets toward any muscle and report back.

So: pull-up target 10 or 8, deadlift 5 or hold at 4 with the recovery reason, and whether the swings are Monday evening by design. Give me those and a yes and I'll record it.
